name: Jackie Auringer
current_role: Construction project manager and marketing professional
bio: Jackie Auringer was born and raised in Kingston, New York. She works as a project manager and managerial accountant in her family's construction business and also works in marketing and branding. She holds a marketing degree and has been active in civic and grassroots political organizing.

platform.point: Lower taxes, energy costs and health care costs for families.
Promote job growth, small businesses, skilled trades and career-connected education.
Strengthen congressional ethics, government transparency and cut wasteful spending.
Protect workers in sectors affected by artificial intelligence.
Suspend AI systems that give weapons-of-mass-destruction instructions, require threat reporting and set federal testing standards.
Backs New York joining the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit for K-12 scholarship donations.
Supports county jail partnerships with ICE and opposes state limits on local cooperation.
Backs a temporary suspension of the federal gas tax.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes, less wasteful spending and relief from regulation and costs on small businesses.

security.evidence: General statement: pledges support for local law enforcement and criticises state limits on sheriffs.

immigration.evidence: Supports Orange County's ICE agreement and county jails holding federal immigration detainees; opposes New York's limits on ICE cooperation.

foreign.evidence: General statement: urged de-escalation and an end to the Iran conflict under an America First framing.

energy.evidence: Backs suspending the federal gas tax and says lowering energy costs is a priority; no climate policy stated.

tech.evidence: Calls for suspending unsafe AI models, mandatory threat reporting, fines and federal testing standards, and backed an AI child-safety bill.

education.evidence: Praised New York's opt-in to the federal tax credit for private K-12 scholarship donations.

notes: The ballot lists her as Jacqueline Auringer. Her press releases were searched; no stated positions were found on abortion, guns, welfare programs or religion in public life.

name: Peter Oberacker
bio: Peter Oberacker has served in the New York State Senate since 2021. He was earlier a Maryland town board member, town supervisor and Otsego County legislator. A food scientist from Schenevus, he founded the food company FormTech Solutions and has been a longtime volunteer firefighter and EMT.

platform.point: Keep taxes low, citing a record of never passing a budget that raised them.
Investigate utility company practices and enact a ratepayer bill of rights.
Ban certain food additives such as Red No. 3 and potassium bromate.
Expand economic opportunity so young people can stay in upstate New York.
Opposes the state energy plan that bans gas stoves in new buildings.
Opposes New York's bail reform law.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on keeping taxes low and never raising them in local budgets.

liberty.evidence: Drugs: voted against 2021 marijuana legalization; abortion and LGBTQ rights: voted no on the 2023 state Equal Rights Amendment (S108A).

security.evidence: Opposes New York's bail reform law.

energy.evidence: Opposes the state energy plan banning gas stoves and campaigns against utility rate hikes.

notes: Searched his campaign site, Senate pages and local news; no stated positions were found on welfare, immigration policy, foreign policy, tech, education or religion.

name: Andrew Garbarino
bio: Andrew Garbarino has represented New York's 2nd District since 2021 and has chaired the House Homeland Security Committee since July 2025. He previously served in the New York State Assembly from 2013 to 2020. He is from Sayville, New York, and is a member of the Republican Governance Group.

platform.point: Leads House Homeland Security Committee work on cybersecurity and infrastructure protection.
Lists standing with law enforcement as an official priority.
Says he works to safeguard constituents' Second Amendment rights.
Names the opioid epidemic as an issue area for his office.
Opposes federal preemption of state animal welfare laws.
Co-chairs the SALT Caucus and sponsored bills to restore the full state and local tax deduction.
Voted for the 2024 Ukraine and Israel security aid packages.
Co-chaired the bipartisan Climate Solutions Caucus and urged FERC to finalise transmission planning rules.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act and sponsored a bill to repeal the estate tax.

welfare.evidence: Voted for final passage of the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which added Medicaid work requirements.

liberty.evidence: Voted for the 2021 background checks bill (guns) and the Respect for Marriage Act (LGBTQ rights).

security.evidence: Voted for passage of the 2024 FISA reauthorization, the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act (H.R. 7888).

immigration.evidence: Voted for the Farm Workforce Modernization Act (2021) and for the Laken Riley Act detention bill (2025).

foreign.evidence: Voted for the 2024 Ukraine and Israel security supplemental appropriations.

energy.evidence: Co-chaired the Climate Solutions Caucus and co-introduced an energy-independence bill; mixed record.

faith.evidence: Co-sponsored the 2021 Fairness for All Act, pairing LGBTQ protections with religious-exercise exemptions.

notes: Scores draw on House roll-call votes and his official issue pages; no clear record was found on tech regulation or school choice.

name: Patrick Halpin
bio: Patrick Halpin served in the Suffolk County Legislature from 1979 and in the New York State Assembly from 1982, then was Suffolk County Executive from 1988 to 1991. He later worked in education nonprofits and served on the Suffolk County Water Authority from 2006, becoming its chair in 2018. He is from Long Island's South Shore.

platform.point: Lower costs for families, from rent and childcare to medical bills.
Oppose tax breaks for billionaires and special interests to help bring costs down.
Expand housing options so young people, families and seniors can stay on Long Island.
Protect drinking water and preserve parks and beaches.
Make community safety a priority, building on his community policing record.
Build toward universal Medicare coverage while protecting existing coverage and lowering drug prices.
Oppose benefit cuts and privatisation of Social Security and Medicare.
Refuses corporate PAC money and supports banning stock trading by members of Congress.

economy.evidence: Says he will fight billionaire tax breaks and special interests to lower costs.

welfare.evidence: Supports building toward universal Medicare coverage while protecting current coverage.

security.evidence: General statement: backs community policing but says ICE agents operate with too little accountability.

immigration.evidence: General statement: wants secure borders and a fixed immigration system, and criticises ICE agents' training and accountability.

energy.evidence: General statement: pledges to make polluters pay and strengthen climate resilience.

notes: Searched his agenda, about and news pages; no positions were found on abortion, guns, foreign policy, tech, school choice or religion. The Wikipedia portrait lacks a specific free licence, so it was not used.

name: Alissa Ellman
current_role: Former U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs program support assistant
bio: Alissa Ellman is the Democratic nominee for New York's 24th District and grew up in Houghton, New York. Her campaign says she worked on flight operations at Bagram Airfield, taught youth in Lockport and worked at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs until being laid off in 2025. She has not held elected office and has also been endorsed by the Forward Party.

platform.point: Protect and expand Medicaid to keep coverage affordable.
Expand child care, fund home repair programs and low-income housing tax credits, and support small businesses.
Extend bus service to rural areas and secure federal funding for water systems and repairs.
Pass the PRO Act, end right-to-work laws and address misclassification of contractors.
Defend LGBTQ rights, marriage equality and reproductive choice.
Reject corporate donations and run a grassroots-funded campaign.
Says America should have a place for anyone who wants to make it their home.

economy.evidence: Supports the PRO Act and ending right-to-work laws.

welfare.evidence: Wants to protect and expand Medicaid and expand child care access.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ: supports LGBTQ rights and marriage equality; abortion: defends reproductive choice.

immigration.evidence: General statement: her issues page says there is a place in America for anyone who wants to call it home.

notes: Searched her issues and about pages and local debate coverage; no positions were found on policing, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: Virginia McIntyre
bio: Virginia McIntyre has served in the Monroe County Legislature since 2024 and is the Republican nominee for New York's 25th District. Born and raised in Gates, she has worked as an entrepreneur, language professor and interpreter, including in Italy. She is a graduate of SUNY Purchase College.

platform.point: End taxes on Social Security, tips and overtime, simplify filing and expand child tax credits.
Back community policing and prevention programs and target trafficking and fentanyl.
Expand vocational and technical education and hold schools accountable.
Require price transparency and protect families from unfair medical billing.
Support congressional term limits, a No Budget, No Pay rule and cutting wasteful spending.
Repair roads and bridges and expand broadband with oversight.
Strengthen access to Medicare and Medicaid.

economy.evidence: Backs the 2025 tax law's cuts for seniors and working families, no tax on tips or overtime, and small-business relief.

welfare.evidence: General statement: pledged to strengthen Medicare and Medicaid access and expand child tax credits.

security.evidence: General statement: supports community policing, prevention programs and targeting trafficking and fentanyl.

notes: Searched her campaign site and launch coverage; no positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, school choice or religion.

name: Jeanine Driscoll
bio: Jeanine Driscoll has been Hempstead Town Receiver of Taxes since 2019 and was re-elected in 2023. She practised aviation law for over two decades and was appointed an associate village justice in Bellerose in 2015. She holds degrees from Catholic University of America and Fordham Law School and lives in Bellerose Village in Nassau County.

platform.point: Restore the full SALT deduction and ease tax burdens on families, seniors and small businesses.
Keep the southern border closed and support record border funding.
Pledges to back law enforcement.
Protect Long Island's aquifer and win federal funding to clean up the Bethpage Plume.
Secure Long Island's share of federal infrastructure money without raising local taxes.
Pursue monetary and fiscal policies to curb inflation and cut regulation on small businesses.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower federal taxes on families and small businesses and backs no tax on tips and overtime.

security.evidence: General statement: pledges to support law enforcement and community safety.

immigration.evidence: Says the southern border must never be opened again and supports record border funding.

notes: Searched her campaign site and Patch questionnaire; no positions were found on abortion, guns, welfare, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: George Marsh
current_role: Former New York City Mayor's Office employee
bio: George Marsh is a candidate for New York's 5th Congressional District in 2026. He grew up in the Astoria Houses in Queens and previously worked in the New York City Mayor's Office. His campaign describes him as a community advocate in Queens.

platform.point: Reintroduce the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to modernise roads, bridges and water systems.
Invest in reliable public transit and safer streets.
Cut red tape and expand access to capital for neighbourhood businesses.
Increase federal funding for apprenticeships and skilled-trades training.
Protect veterans' benefits and expand employment and housing services.

economy.evidence: General statements: wants more federal infrastructure and community investment, alongside less red tape for small businesses.

notes: His campaign site lists a Queens United independent line for November; it states no positions on the other nine topics, and web searches found no questionnaires or news coverage.
